
# Voice Bibles

These rules govern every written player-facing word: barks, quest text, item descriptions, store copy, notifications, error messages. Rules carry IDs so a verdict can cite them.

## Emberwake — weathered, wry, plainspoken

The world has burned before and the people in it know it. They are tired, competent, and quietly funny.

- **EW-1** Plainspoken first. Short words, short sentences. If a line needs a comma splice to land, cut it in half instead.
- **EW-2** No modern slang, no internet cadence. Nothing a player could screenshot as "the game talking like a feed."
- **EW-3** No exclamation stacking. One `!` per line at most; none in item descriptions.
- **EW-4** Wry means understatement, not jokes. A character may notice the absurd; they never perform for the player.
- **EW-5** Death, loss, and fire are real. Never wink at them.

**Emberwake banned words:** awesome, epic (as praise — the rarity tier is fine), literally, vibes, boss (as address), buddy, folks, super (as intensifier), gonna, gotta, hey there.

## Drift Harbor — warm, unhurried

Nothing in the harbor is an emergency. The game's voice is a neighbor who is glad you came by.

- **DH-1** Warm and unhurried. Lines can breathe; a gentle sentence beats a punchy one.
- **DH-2** No combat metaphors. Nothing is killed, targeted, conquered, dominated, or crushed — including in UI copy about goals and records.
- **DH-3** No urgency language. Never "hurry," "last chance," "act now," "don't miss," or a countdown framing. Timed content is described by when it ends, not by what the player might lose.
- **DH-4** Second person is an invitation, not an instruction. "You could…" over "You must…"
- **DH-5** One `!` per line at most, and only for genuine delight.

**Drift Harbor banned words:** kill, destroy, attack, target, grind, deadline, fail, hurry, unlock (use "open up"), warning, error (player-facing — say what happened instead), fire (the noun — the harbor does not burn).

## Length limits (both titles)

| Text type | Limit | Counted how |
| --- | --- | --- |
| VO bark | ≤ 9 words | hyphenated compounds count as one word |
| Subtitle line | ≤ 42 characters | spaces and punctuation included; placeholders at longest known expansion |
| Notification body | ≤ 90 characters | same counting as subtitles |

Limits are voice rules: an over-limit line fails with the limit and the actual count cited.

## The same beat in both voices

| Beat | Emberwake | Drift Harbor |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A storm is coming | "Storm's coming. Same as the last one we outlived." | "Clouds rolling in over the bay. A good day for the workshop." |
| Player returns after absence | "Back, then. The road keeps what it keeps." | "Welcome back. The gulls saved your spot on the pier." |
| New content available | "There's work east of the ridge, if you want it." | "Something new washed in with the tide. Come see when you like." |

Read the pairs before writing either title: the Emberwake line earns warmth by withholding it; the Drift Harbor line has nothing to withhold.
